name: VW (VON WILLEBRAND ) FACTOR ANTIGEN
interpretation:
Note
1.Individuals of Blood Group “O” may have lower vWF antigen than those of other ABO blood groups.
2.The presence of Rheumatoid factor may lead to underestimation of the vWF antigen.
3.Test conducted on Citrated plasma.
Comments
Von Willebrand factor plays a key role in Primary & Secondary hemostasis. In the latter role it serves as a carrier protein for Factor VIII. It is the most common inherited bleeding disorder characterized by easy bruising and prolonged bleeding from mucosal surfaces.

Classification of von Willebrand disease

TYPE REMARKS
1 Partial quantitative deficiency of vWF
2 Qualitative deficiency of VWF
2A Decreased platelet dependent vWF function with selective deficiency of High molecular weight multimers
2B Increased affinity for platelet glycoprotein 1b
2M Decreased platelet dependent vWF function with normal High molecular weight multimers
2N Markedly decreased binding of Factor VIII to vWF
3 Complete deficiency of vWF

Decreased levels

  • Hereditary
  • Acquired - Monoclonal gammopathies, Lymphoproliferative disorders, Autoimmune disorders and Hypothyroidism.

Increased levels
Pregnancy, Acute illness, Exercise, Liver Disease, Vasculitis, Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura.

Interpretation :
1. Von Willebrand factor (vWF) is an adhesive protein synthesized by the endothelial cells and megakaryocytes.
2. It plays an important role in the adhesion of platelets to the sub-endothelium and in platelet aggregation.
3. Von Willebrand disease (vWD) is the most common hereditary coagulation abnormality described in humans.
4. It arises from a qualitative or quantitative deficiency of von Willebrand factor (vWF).
5. High concentrations have been associated with certain inflammatory or atherosclerotic vascular incidents as well as stress, pregnancy, oral contraception, severe hepatic disease etc.
